transcript:
Meeting header
Date/Time: 2027-08-09 16:30 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Aisha (Tidewell CTO), Luis (Lead ML), Priya (SecEng)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everybody, thanks for making time. i'm maya from redwood, i'm the ae on the account. quick round robin?
[00:08] Aisha Rahman: thanks maya, i'm aisha, cto at tidewell. we're exploring inference for our customer-facing agent and some doc ingest features.
[00:15] Luis Ortega: hi all, luis, i run ml infra, curious about latencies and cost curves.
[00:20] Priya Nair: priya here—security and compliance for integrations.
[00:24] Ethan Park: Ethan, redwood se, i'll cover the pilot and benchmarks side.

[00:30] Maya Chen: great. high level — are you leaning self-serve hosted first, or do you need dedicated / private right away?
[00:36] Aisha Rahman: we were hoping to start self-serve to prove concept, but there are compliance constraints for PII and some data residency asks. so we want a path to private if pilot looks good.
[00:47] Luis Ortega: also, what's realistic ttft — time to first token — we want to show PMs something in a week.

[00:55] Ethan Park: absolutely. our quickstart is typically minutes to first token for simple requests. for more real workloads with your doc sizes and kv cache warmup, plan for a couple hours to get stable metrics, but you can demo basic generation in <30 mins. note: sometimes our auto-transcripts say "kv cash" or similar, the se will show KV cache examples.

[01:20] Priya Nair: can you summarize security posture? we need SOC 2, SAML, KMS, audit logs, and ability to keep keys in our HSM, ideally.
[01:32] Maya Chen: yes — we provide SOC 2 report, SSO via SAML/OIDC, and for Private we support customer-managed KMS/HSM integration. hosted customers can use Redwood-managed KMS with additional encryption-at-rest controls. audit logs and token-level tracing are in the console. we'll send the whitepaper.

[01:58] Aisha Rahman: ok, good. another Q: cost vs latency — if we go hosted and use a smaller model, might be cheaper but higher latency?
[02:06] Ethan Park: tradeoffs: hosted gives fastest on-ramp and predictable pay-as-you-go. Dedicated (reserved GPU) has predictable throughput and lower per-token cost at scale. Private (VPC or on-prem) gives you control over data residency and KMS, but longer lead time. model size, quantization, and batching affect latency/cost — we can recommend quantization profiles after seeing your token distribution.

[02:35] Luis Ortega: do you support continuous batching and prefix caching? we have a lot of repeated prompts across sessions.
[02:42] Ethan Park: yes — our runtime supports continuous batching and KV cache warmup. we can show how prefix caching reduces token counts and apparent latency. there's also an Optimize profile we can run that suggests batching configs.

[03:05] Maya Chen: timeline — what are you hoping to accomplish in the pilot?
[03:10] Aisha Rahman: validate that we can hit p95 latency <250ms on short conversational queries and cost per 1,000 requests under $X (we'll share exact target). second, prove a secure flow for PII handling and key management.

[03:27] Luis Ortega: also want to test throughput up to about 200 rps in burst for a small subset.

[03:33] Ethan Park: that sounds doable. for p95 <250ms we may recommend a smaller low-latency model variant or dedicated pool. we'll sketch two approaches: 1) Hosted quickstart with free credits to validate functionality & TTFT, 2) Dedicated pilot to validate p95 and throughput with reserved GPUs and autoscaling.

[03:57] Priya Nair: about free credits — what's typical? we need enough to run our bench for two weeks.
[04:03] Maya Chen: typical pilot credits vary — we usually offer enough to run a 2–4 week pilot depending on expected volume. i'll propose a credits package and a pricing playbook in the follow-up.

[04:20] Aisha Rahman: does Redwood provide sample benchmark scripts? we prefer something reproducible.
[04:25] Ethan Park: yes — we'll share a benchmark repo, sample load script, and a pre-seeded tenant with sample prompt sets. the repo includes latency, token accounting, and cost estimate helpers.

[04:40] Luis Ortega: are there any gotchas with SDKs? we use python + node.
[04:45] Ethan Park: SDKs for python and node, plus curl examples. there's occasional mismatch between streaming behavior and some frameworks — we'll include a streaming example and troubleshooting notes. also mention: if you need to call external tools, we support function calling style payloads.

[05:10] Aisha Rahman: ok. on private deployment — what's realistic lead time to get a VPC private pilot?
[05:15] Maya Chen: VPC deployment typically is 4–6 weeks for initial setup (network peering, customer KMS, firewall rules) if nothing else blocks it. on-prem takes longer. if you need faster validation, start hosted self-serve while we begin private onboarding in parallel.

[05:36] Priya Nair: any SOC 2 or contract redlines we should expect? e.g., data retention and deletion terms?
[05:42] Maya Chen: we have standard terms and enterprise addenda for retention, deletion, and data processing. we'll share the SOC2 report and standard security brochure. for strict retention controls we recommend Private deployment.

[06:00] Luis Ortega: curious about model variants and fallbacks — if we pin a model and there's capacity pressure, do you auto-fallback?
[06:07] Ethan Park: yes — we support smart routing policies. you can pin model versions and set fallback rules to compatible variants (smaller model) with alerting. useful for graceful degradation during bursty traffic.

[06:25] Aisha Rahman: demo or walkthrough request — would be helpful to see the console's trace view and token cost breakdown.
[06:32] Maya Chen: we'll include console screenshots in the follow-up and schedule a walkthrough with the product analytics dash.

[06:40] Luis Ortega: does Redwood measure tokenization differences for multilingual prompts? we have Spanish/English mix.
[06:44] Ethan Park: tokenization is included in cost metrics. for mixed languages, the tokenization can shift. we'll run sample tokenization checks for your expected payloads.

[06:58] Maya Chen: let's scope the pilot: 6 weeks, start hosted quickstart for TTFT and functional validation in week 1, run benchmarks week 2–3, optionally spin up dedicated pool in week 4 if p95 targets not met, and continue to private onboarding in parallel if compliance checks pass.

[07:20] Aisha Rahman: that plan sounds reasonable. Luis will lead the benchmark work. Priya will own the security checklist.

[07:28] Priya Nair: on KMS — if we keep keys in our HSM, what's the path?
[07:32] Ethan Park: for private, we can do customer-managed KMS with HSM integration. hosted supports bring-your-own-KMS with limited options today; for full HSM we usually recommend VPC/private. we'll include an architecture diagram in the follow up that shows the key flows.

[07:54] Maya Chen: any blockers or hard requirements we should know about today?
[07:58] Aisha Rahman: two big items — minimum p95 latency and the legal team's need to see SOC2 + data flow diagrams.

[08:06] Maya Chen: understood. we'll include both in the packet.

[08:12] Luis Ortega: can the trial tenant be preloaded with our doc embeddings so we can test reranking and retrieval-augmented generation?
[08:18] Ethan Park: yes, we can pre-seed a tenant with embeddings and show reranker configs. note: sometimes embeddings and reranking require tuning — we'll add a sample evaluation harness.

[08:33] Priya Nair: logging and audit — is token-level tracing stored, and for how long?
[08:38] Maya Chen: default retention is 30 days for hosted; enterprise packages can extend retention or forward logs to your syslog/Splunk. for private, retention is under your control.

[08:52] Aisha Rahman: what's the expected onboarding effort for our engs?
[08:55] Ethan Park: for basic self-serve it's low — sign up, grab API key, run a couple of curl/python examples and you're at TTFT. for dedicated/private there's more coordination: network setup, IAM, and keys. we'll provide runbooks and a SE to help.

[09:12] Maya Chen: any specific benchmarks you want us to run?
[09:15] Luis Ortega: p95 latency, token cost per request, throughput at 200 rps for 60s bursts, and model output quality for our prompts.

[09:23] Ethan Park: noted. we'll include instructions for measuring p95 and orchestrating burst tests to avoid noisy neighbors in hosted. for deterministic latencies we'll show the dedicated plan.

[09:40] (cross-talk)
[09:43] Aisha Rahman: one more: who at Redwood will be our day-to-day contact during pilot?
[09:47] Maya Chen: me for account/credits, ethan for technical and benchmarks. you'll have a shared channel we can use for quick questions.

[09:55] Priya Nair: any precedent customers in our regulatory space?
[09:59] Maya Chen: yes — we've worked with healthtech and fintech customers; i'll point you to anonymized references and case studies.

[10:10] Luis Ortega: for the sample benchmark, can you include an example of quantization profiles and expected cost delta?
[10:15] Ethan Park: yes — the Optimize recommendations will include model/quantization suggestions and cost per 1k tokens for those variants.

[10:28] Aisha Rahman: ok, let's recap next steps briefly.
[10:31] Maya Chen: recap: Redwood to provision trial tenant + sample prompts + benchmark scripts; send SOC2 and architecture whitepaper; propose credits amount and pricing scenarios; schedule benchmark session week of Aug 16. Customer to try self-serve and give TTFT feedback.

[10:52] Priya Nair: i'll put together compliance questions.

[10:55] Maya Chen: perfect. any final Qs?
[10:58] Luis Ortega: none from me, thanks.
[11:00] Aisha Rahman: thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.

[11:05] Maya Chen: thanks all — we'll follow up with the packet and calendar invites.

End of transcript

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard tokens ("kv cash", "redwood dedicate") and filler words are present. The content maps to a 48min call with a concise discovery and explicit next steps.
notes: Pilot scoped as hosted quickstart -> optional dedicated -> parallel private onboarding. Emphasis on TTFT, SOC2, KMS/HSM, p95 latency. Redwood to provide trial tenant, benchmark scripts, SOC2 + whitepaper, pricing scenarios and credits proposal. SE will run benchmark with customer's ML lead.
